...
## Start with the mattress type

This is the biggest decision you'll make because it determines how the mattress will feel. You can often find different firmness levels available for each type of mattress.

- Memory foam: This is the most popular type of mattress on the market. It’s made of synthetic foams and provides exceptional pressure relief. The foam adapts to your body shape so you feel like you're being cradled, making it great for side sleepers or people with back pain. Just note that memory foam is known to trap heat and isn’t as durable as other materials.
- Innerspring (or coils): Primarily made up of metal springs on the inside, they're usually firmer, have more bounce, and tend to be more durable than other mattress types. Plus, innersprings allow for more breathability so they often sleep cooler. These mattresses are ideal for stomach sleepers and heavier body weights.
- Latex: It offers more cushioning than innersprings, but it’s more resilient than foam, making you feel more like you’re lying on top of the mattress instead of sinking-in. Latex is made from the sap of rubber trees and may be used in organic mattresses, so they're also ideal for eco-conscious shoppers. The downside is latex is typically more expensive, heavier to maneuver, and may be too firm for some.
- Hybrid: These combine memory foam or latex and coils for the benefits (and downsides) of both. The surface uses foam for comfort, while the bottom incorporates the coils for support. Hybrids tend to be more expensive than their all-foam counterparts.
...
## Factor in your sleep position and body type

The goal is to keep your spine in neutral alignment, so factoring in how you sleep can help narrow down your search. Stomach sleepers need a firm mattress, side sleepers should opt for a softer surface to avoid stress on the pressure points like your shoulders, hips, and knees, and back sleepers (and anyone who changes positions) would fall somewhere in between at a medium firmness.

Body type matters, too. Heavier bodies need a firmer bed for support, while lightweight frames are better suited with a softer mattress.
...
Mattress height affects both comfort and convenience, and most models fall between 10 and 15 inches tall. Shorter mattresses (around 10 to 11 inches) are often easier to maneuver (because they're lighter in weight) and may cost less. Taller mattresses (14 inches and higher) tend to feel more luxurious because they can incorporate additional comfort layers, and they may be easier to get in and out of. Just keep in mind that taller mattresses are typically heavier, more expensive and may require deep-pocket sheets.

## Don't get too hung up on sales

One thing I've learned after more than a decade of testing mattresses: Most brands are almost always running some sort of promotion. Rather than focusing on the advertised percentage discount, pay attention to the actual selling price. A 40% discount isn't necessarily a better deal than a 15% discount if the final price is higher.

## How to shop for a mattress

There isn't one model that's best for everyone, so it's important to think about your personal needs when shopping for a mattress. Here's what to consider before you buy:
...
✔️ Sleep position: The goal is to keep your spine in neutral alignment, so factoring in how you sleep can help narrow down your search. Stomach sleepers need a firm mattress, side sleepers should opt for a softer surface to avoid stress on the pressure points like your shoulders, hips and knees, and back sleepers (and anyone who changes positions) would fall somewhere in between at a medium firmness.

✔️ Body type: Heavy people need a firmer bed for support, while lightweight frames are better suited with a softer mattress. Take into account both your weight and sleep position when deciding on the right firmness level.

✔️ Back pain: If you suffer from lower or upper back pain, look for a pressure-relieving mattress with all foam or a hybrid of foam and coils. Medical experts also advise looking for medium firmness for a balance of cushioning and support.
...
✔️ Temperature: Hot sleepers or anyone dealing with night sweats would benefit from a mattress with cooling properties. Memory foam tends to sleep hot, so look for a mattress with coils for airflow or cooling technology like copper particles, gel or phase change technology that's added to the foam.

✔️ Trial period: It's difficult to know whether a mattress is a good fit without actually sleeping on it. Fortunately, most mattress companies offer an any-reason return period for at least 100 nights. Before you buy, check whether there are any hidden return fees and how you go about making the return to avoid any headaches later on.

The general assistants are powerful, but they weren’t built with keyword clustering and content calendars in mind. The marketing-focused tools fill that gap, and several have evolved far beyond simple copy generators. The best ones now run a loop from research to brief to draft to optimization without you having to stitch three different apps together.

### Jasper
...
enterprise content teams, branded marketing at volume

Used by Akbank, Adidas, and Cushman & Wakefield. Jasper’s Brand Voice feature is genuinely impressive. It reads your existing content, infers your tone and style, and then maintains that consistency across everything it generates.

Over 50 templates cover the standard marketing content types. The Kanban-style campaign manager is a genuine productivity gain for teams. It’s expensive, and it’s ultimately GPT under the hood, but the workflow layer earns its price for content operations at scale.
...
### Surfer SEO
...
SEO-first content teams, anyone writing for organic search traffic

Surfer remains the gold standard for on-page SEO writing support. In 2026, its most important evolution is its move toward Answer Engine Optimization (AEO). It now helps structure content to appear in AI-generated search overviews, not just traditional Google results. For any team whose traffic depends on organic search, Surfer isn’t optional; it’s infrastructure.

The points-based scoring system makes optimization accessible even for writers who have never opened a keyword research tool.

### Copy.ai
...
high-volume short-form copy, automated marketing workflows

The king of short-form. Perfect for high-volume social media posts, ad copy, and Workflows that automate your entire content calendar.

Copy.ai’s Workflows feature has become one of its main attractions. You can automate entire content pipelines, from prospect research to personalized outreach to social posts, without writing a line of code. For a marketing team running dozens of campaigns simultaneously, the time savings are substantial. It won’t produce your brand’s most nuanced long-form content, but that was never the point.

## Creative and fiction writing

This is where the tool market gets genuinely interesting and where most general-purpose assistants fall flat. Writing fiction isn’t about producing grammatically correct text. It’s about sustaining tension, building character interiority, managing pacing across hundreds of pages, and generating descriptive language that doesn’t read like a product listing. The creative writing tools understand this distinction in a way that ChatGPT, for all its versatility, simply doesn’t.

### Sudowrite
...
fiction writers of any level, from hobbyists to publishing professionals

The most purpose-built fiction tool in the market. Sudowrite’s Story Engine can outline entire novels, and its Describe function generates sensory scene descriptions across specific senses. You can ask it to render a scene through smell alone or through sound. Its Canvas feature provides a bird’s-eye view of your manuscript structure. The Write button, which generates the next 300 words when you’re stuck, is simple in concept and wildly effective in practice.

writers who want proofreading without personality erasure

The distinction that makes editGPT worth knowing: most AI editing tools optimize for correctness, and in doing so, they sand away everything that makes your voice your voice. editGPT uses a Track Changes-style interface so you can review every proposed alteration and keep or reject it.

It catches what needs catching, such as structural issues, clarity problems, and clunky phrasing, without turning a writer’s distinctive style into sanitized AI-speak. For writers who care deeply about their voice, that restraint is the whole product.

Scrivener is, first and foremost, a manuscript management tool; it has been so for two decades. Its 2026 AI plugins don’t try to write your book for you. Instead, they help you maintain internal consistency across a 90,000-word manuscript: tracking character descriptions, flagging plot-hole candidates, checking that your fictional world’s rules haven’t contradicted themselves.

For serious long-form writers, this is an organizational layer that no general-purpose chatbot can replicate.

# The Best Writing Model Saves the Edit

The best LLM for writing is a task-based shortlist. Start with three current models, then compare factual failures, constraint failures, and editing time.
...
As of September 22, 2026, start with Claude Sonnet 5 for drafting and voice-sensitive editing, GPT-5.6 Terra for tightly constrained variants, and Gemini 3.8 Flash for source-heavy synthesis.

We have not run a creative-writing test that proves one is universally best. If you want one first trial, begin with Sonnet 5, then compare its failures and editing time with the other two on the same brief.

We checked the current provider documentation before making that shortlist. Those pages establish context limits, input types, reasoning modes, and tools. They do not establish whose prose wins a blind review.

That distinction repairs the old version of this article. A broad capability score can help build a shortlist. It cannot turn instruction following into taste, a context window into continuity, or a knowledge score into fewer errors on your article.

## Three current models worth testing

Table 1

Model | What the provider documents | Our editorial starting point | What can make it lose 
---|---|---|---
Claude Sonnet 5 | Anthropic lists content creation among its use cases. The current model has adaptive thinking, a 1M-token context window, and a 128K maximum output. | Start here for long-form drafting and edits where the source voice must survive. | The provider evidence does not measure voice preservation. A rigid template or source-heavy workflow may favor another candidate. 
GPT-5.6 Terra | OpenAI documents reasoning, structured outputs, file search, web search, a 1.05M-token context window, and a 128K maximum output. | Start here for marketing variants and technical drafts with hard fields, sections, or output rules. | Structure can pass while the prose still sounds wrong. API capabilities also do not prove that a consumer ChatGPT plan exposes the same route or tools. 
Gemini 3.8 Flash | Google documents text, image, video, audio, and PDF input, plus file search, URL context, search grounding, structured output, and a 1,048,576-token input limit. | Start here when the writing job begins with a mixed-format source pack. | A large input limit and grounding tools do not guarantee correct citations, complete source recall, or an acceptable voice. 

The shortlist is deliberately small. It gives you one plausible first model for each workflow without dressing provider specifications as a prose leaderboard.

## Best for specific writing tasks

### Blog posts and long-form articles

Start with Claude Sonnet 5 when the job is an outline, a source pack, and several sections that need one voice. Anthropic explicitly names content creation as a Sonnet 5 use case, so it belongs in the trial. That is capability evidence, not a finding that its drafts are better.

Run GPT-5.6 Terra beside it when the article has a strict template, required fields, or output that must feed another system. Add Gemini 3.8 Flash when the source pack mixes PDFs, URLs, images, and text. Sonnet loses if it takes longer to repair structure or source handling than either alternative.

### Editing and rewriting

Claude Sonnet 5 is our first trial for voice-preserving edits. The test is narrow: give it the original, the style rules, and a list of sentences or facts it may not change. Then inspect every unnecessary rewrite.

Do not ask which output sounds most polished in isolation. Compare each edit with the source voice. Count altered claims, deleted qualifiers, new cliches, and minutes needed to restore the author's choices. Terra should join the trial when the requested edits can be expressed as hard constraints. It wins if fewer off-limits sentences move.

### Copywriting and marketing

Start with GPT-5.6 Terra for a batch that needs fixed fields such as audience, offer, proof, objection, and call to action. Structured output can keep those fields inspectable. It does not make the copy persuasive.

Hold the offer and evidence constant across models. Reject a variant that invents proof, drops a required qualifier, or changes the offer. Blind-review the survivors for voice and message clarity. Sonnet 5 is the useful counterweight when brand voice matters more than machine-readable structure.

### Email newsletters and outreach

Use the same comparison for email rather than assuming the fastest generator is the cheapest workflow. Ask Terra and Gemini 3.8 Flash for the same number of variants, with the same audience segments and prohibited claims. Count duplicates, unsupported personalization, and edits per accepted message.

results.summary:
- Best overall stack (our pick): DeepSeek drafts → ChatGPT revises → human edits and fact-checks. No single model beats that combination.

One note on how we judge this: benchmarks are useful for lab tasks, but what you actually need from a writing model is strong first drafts that don't read like template filler, tone flexibility, structural thinking, and long-form coherence. That's the lens for everything below.

## What We're Comparing (and What We're Not)

Benchmarks are useful for lab tasks, but content writing is a different animal. What you actually need from a writing model is:

- Strong first drafts that don't read like template filler
- Tone flexibility — can it sound like your brand, not like an AI?
- Structural thinking — outlines, logical flow, scannable sections
- Long-form coherence — does it stay on-topic at 2,000 words, or drift?

So let's compare the majors on those axes.

## ChatGPT: The Reliable All-Rounder

ChatGPT remains the default for a reason. Its strength for content writers is consistency: it follows style instructions well, handles tone requests ("make this punchier, less corporate") reliably, and produces clean, well-structured output across formats — blog posts, email sequences, ad copy, landing page headlines.

Its long-form coherence is solid, though very long pieces can still get repetitive or hedge-y in the middle. And its biggest weakness is the one every model shares: a tendency toward safe, generic phrasing that needs a human edit to bring to life.

Best for: final revisions, tone polishing, headline and subject line variations, and any task where following precise style instructions matters.

## Claude: Excellent Prose, With One Caveat

Claude is widely regarded as one of the best pure writers among the major models. Its prose tends to be more natural and less listicle-brained — it often produces drafts that need less "de-AI-ing" than competitors.

However, content writers should be aware of a growing concern: Claude's watermarking behavior. For marketers whose content needs to pass through AI detectors, client review, or publishing platforms with originality requirements, this is worth testing for your own use case before you commit your workflow to it. If you're producing content where AI-detection matters — ghostwriting, some freelance contexts, certain editorial standards — it's a factor to weigh.
...
natural-sounding long-form drafts, narrative content, and pieces where conversational voice matters most.

## Gemini: Strong Structure, Google-Native Advantages

Gemini's writing quality has improved dramatically, and its structural output — outlines, section breakdowns, content briefs — is among the best. If your workflow starts with research and planning, Gemini is a strong choice for the front end of the process.

For raw prose, it still tends to run slightly more formal and formulaic than Claude or a well-prompted ChatGPT, and long-form pieces can occasionally lose momentum. But its integration with research tools makes it valuable for the ideation and outline stages.
...
content briefs, outlines, research synthesis, and structurally complex pieces.

## DeepSeek: The Underrated Drafting Machine

DeepSeek is the sleeper pick of 2026 for content workflows. Its drafting output is fast, surprisingly creative, and — critically — it tends to produce drafts that feel less polished-but-generic and more exploratory. That sounds like a flaw. For drafting, it's a feature.

Here's the insight: a first draft's job is not to be good. A first draft's job is to give you material. A model that produces slightly rougher, more varied prose gives you more to work with than one that produces uniformly competent-but-bland copy. And DeepSeek's speed and cost profile make it painless to generate multiple draft angles and pick the best one.
...
high-volume first drafts, exploring multiple angles quickly, and getting past the blank page.

## The Workflow We've Found Works Best: DeepSeek Drafts, ChatGPT Revises

Here's our key finding after working across these models: the winning stack isn't one model — it's DeepSeek for drafting and ChatGPT for final revision.

Why this combination works:

- DeepSeek generates raw material fast. You can produce three or four draft approaches to a piece without friction, which means you're never married to a weak opening. Optionality is the most underrated asset in content creation.
- ChatGPT excels at instruction-following during revision. Revision is a different task than drafting. It requires precision: "cut this section by 30%, keep the tone conversational, tighten every sentence." ChatGPT follows those constraints more reliably than any other model we'...

## Come scegliere il giusto generatore di contenuti AI

Scegliere lo strumento di AI per i contenuti giusto può fare una grande differenza nell’efficienza con cui crei contenuti e raggiungi i tuoi obiettivi. Quando valuti gli strumenti di scrittura AI, concentrati su questi fattori chiave che possono aiutarti a trovare la soluzione più adatta alle tue esigenze, che si tratti di scrivere contenuti SEO con l’AI, post per i social media o testi di marketing.

Ecco come decidere.

### 1. Valuta il tuo budget

I piani gratuiti di strumenti come ChatGPT e Claude sono sorprendentemente validi e ti permettono di generare rapidamente contenuti di qualità. Tuttavia, raggiungono rapidamente i limiti di utilizzo se crei più contenuti in una settimana.

Nel frattempo, gli strumenti che usano un sistema di crediti come 1minAI possono essere convenienti per i piccoli progetti, ma sono meno pratici per i contenuti complessi che richiedono più revisioni.

In base alla mia esperienza, se produci più di tre o quattro contenuti a settimana, vale la pena fare l’upgrade e prevedere nel budget almeno un piano da 20 €/mese per mantenere l’efficienza ed evitare di raggiungere i limiti.

### 2. Scegli in base al tipo di contenuto

Gli strumenti in grado di gestire una comunicazione bidirezionale e prompt conversazionali, come ChatGPT e Claude, sono ideali per contenuti lunghi e approfonditi — post del blog, articoli o testi ricchi di ricerca — perché posso perfezionare l’output al volo.

D’altra parte, gli strumenti che si basano su prompt più semplici funzionano bene come spunti iniziali per brevi testi di marketing, post sui social o sessioni di brainstorming.

Quando scegli uno strumento, pensa ai contenuti che crei più spesso, così puoi sceglierne uno che renda quei flussi di lavoro il più fluidi possibile.

### 3. Valuta la facilità d’uso

Per la mia esperienza, più uno strumento è facile da usare, più riesco a concentrarmi sulla creazione di contenuti invece di cercare di capire come funziona la piattaforma.

Cerco interfacce intuitive, modelli predefiniti e integrazioni con strumenti che uso già ‒ come Google Docs, WordPress o Canva ‒ perché mi permettono di passare senza interruzioni dalla ricerca alla stesura e alla pubblicazione.

Funzionalità come un editor di testo avanzato con funzioni AI integrate, tasti di scelta rapida o barre degli strumenti pop-up possono farti risparmiare minuti (o ore) ogni giorno, soprattutto quando lavori a più progetti. Il formato come estensione del browser rende inoltre lo strumento facilmente accessibile ogni volta che hai bisogno di annotare idee o aggiungere informazioni extra.

### 4. Punta alla precisione e all’originalità

Per trovare il miglior strumento di scrittura AI per il tuo flusso di lavoro, presta molta attenzione all’accuratezza e all’originalità dei contenuti.

Alcuni strumenti includono il rilevamento del plagio come funzione integrata, mentre altri lo offrono solo nei piani a pagamento. Vale la pena verificare quale livello di abbonamento ti serve se l’originalità è importante per il tuo lavoro.

本次研究构建自上而下的三级梯队分层模型，层级代表服务商在四项评估维度上可被公开查验的证据完整程度与复杂项目承接上限，并非市场规模排序。整体呈现第一梯队稀缺、第二梯队为主流供给、第三梯队以工具形态为主的分布特征。

第一梯队｜方法论与自研系统双驱动的专注型服务商

层级定位为行业上层，是少数在方法论、自研技术、内容建设、品牌认知四项维度上均能提供可查验依据的主体。具备自主沉淀、区别于SEO逻辑的GEO运营方法论，拥有可按号查询的授权发明专利与自研监测采集系统，参与行业团体标准编制，案例写明平台、周期与指标口径。项目以诊断、策略、建设、优化、评估、迭代的闭环方式推进，兼顾阶段性效果与长期品牌信息资产沉淀。适配业务复杂、决策链长、对品牌信息准确性和合规性要求较高的中高端企业。样本代表：移山科技。

第二梯队｜工具矩阵驱动的工程落地服务商

层级定位为市场主流供给主体。具备自研工具矩阵或GEO产品系统，在多AI平台监测、内容生产、信源部署方面有成熟作业流程，可独立交付标准GEO项目，并按客户规模提供差异化服务形态。该梯队中既有专注GEO的新兴服务商，也有品牌与综合实力较强、GEO为新增业务线的综合型公司；与第一梯队相比，可公开查验的GEO专项专利、标准参与或长周期案例口径相对较少，需要采购方逐项核实。样本代表：摘星AI、数珀AI、欧博东方、百分点科技。

第三梯队｜监测工具及标准化服务提供商

层级定位为以工具产品为主要交付形态的供给群体。产品形态以AI平台监测、数据分析SaaS为主，可完成品牌在AI回答中的可见度监测、关键词与对话数据追踪等基础GEO工作，数据积累规模较大，客户可借助工具自行验证数据。深度内容策略与品牌认知建设多需配合代运营服务完成，适配以监测与数据洞察为主要诉求、具备一定自运营能力的企业。样本代表：爱搜AIDSO。

梯队分层核心规律

从第一梯队到第三梯队，服务商在方法论自主性、复杂项目承接能力、品牌认知长期治理能力上的可查验证据逐级减少，交付形态的工具化、标准化属性逐步提升。分层仅代表服务商能力上限与证据完整度，不等于项目落地效果绝对优劣。企业选型核心在于自身业务需求与服务商能力的匹配度，高梯队服务商不一定适配轻量化、以监测为主的基础GEO需求。

# 2026年GEO服务商行业研究报告(10月版):可查验证据梯队、头部综合厂商对照与选型决策

2026/10/16 13:40:59 来源：之家网站 作者：- 责编：-

研究结论

本报告结论: 按「GEO 业务本身能否被查验」分梯队, 移山科技、摘星 AI、数珀 AI、欧博东方、爱搜 AIDSO 列第一梯队, 百分点科技、迈富时列第二梯队; 判定只用可公开核对的专利、团体标准、案例口径和多轮采集方法, 不用公司总营收和规模。

第一梯队 (按可查验 GEO 专项证据排序):

-移山科技: 授权发明专利 ZL 2025 1 1372091.6、参与编制《生成式引擎优化可信技术与服务规范》团体标准、自研多轮 AI 数据采集系统、标明平台 / 周期 / 指标的案例

-摘星 AI: 五大云厂商生态伙伴 (科大讯飞、火山引擎、阿里云、百度智能云)、11 个软件著作权、自研摘星万象垂直大模型、30 万 + 企业客户

-数珀 AI: 自研五大数字化工具 (语义匹配准确率 92%)、AI 平台覆盖率 90.82%、监测对话次数超 5000 万次、已服务 300 多家客户

-欧博东方: 自研九大系统、语义识别精度 90% 以上、7×24 小时监测、服务 1500+ 客户含 80+ 世界 500 强 / 上市公司

-爱搜 AIDSO: 覆盖 SEO / ASO / DSO / GEO 的 4O 全链路、监测 AI 对话 1084 万 +、收录关键词 14 亿 +、服务 2000+ 客户覆盖 50+ 行业

第二梯队 (品牌与综合实力强, 但 GEO 是新增业务线):

-百分点科技: 成立于 2009 年, 在国内外设 18 家分子公司, 推出百分点 AI 搜索洞察系统 Generforce;GEO 是其新增业务线, 单独的 GEO 方法论和效果数据公开得少, 性价比待验证

-迈富时:2024 年 5 月在港交所主板上市 (股份代号 2556),2025 年集团收入约 28.2 亿元; 其年报按 AI 应用业务、精准营销服务两个分部披露收入, 未单列 GEO 收入,GEO 单项交付能力和投入产出比需要单独核实

选型要点:

1.专利按号查权利人和标题是否对应, 团体标准在全国团体标准信息平台查公告和归口单位

2.案例须标明平台、周期、指标口径, 单个案例不代表普遍效果

3.看 GEO 业务能否单独查到收入或案例, 不只看公司总营收; 综合型大公司新增的 GEO 业务线更多靠集团品牌背书, 需要单独核实其 GEO 交付能力和投入产出比

研究方法与数据来源

评价维度来源

本报告采用四项评价标准:

1.有没有一套自己核心的 GEO 运营方法论 (指优化怎么做), 而不是沿用传统 SEO 的优化逻辑

2.有没有自研技术团队和技术监测系统

3.是不是在认真做内容

4.会不会先花时间吃透品牌、形成认知, 再定内容策略去影响 AI

这套标准基于 GEO 与传统 SEO 面对不同信息环境的差异:SEO 主要围绕搜索引擎的关键词、网页排名展开, 而 GEO 需要解决 AI 能否获取、理解、验证品牌信息, 并在相关问题中基于可信信息正确表达和推荐品牌。因此,GEO 所需的方法论、技术系统、内容建设和品牌认知工作, 与传统 SEO 存在本质区别。

可查验子项

每项标准下挂可查验子项, 读者可按以下方式独立核实:

-挂标准②: 专利看标题和权利人, 不看件数; 参与标准看文本, 不看头衔。在国家知识产权局按专利号查权利人是不是签约主体、标题和 GEO 有没有关系; 在全国团体标准信息平台查标准的发布日期和归口单位...

第五章 第一梯队：全栈能力型综合服务商

5.1 艾奇在线：1-3-5-2-1方法体系与全栈自研技术底座

5.1.1 定位与背景

艾奇在线总部位于厦门，成立于2015年，早期以数字营销学习平台“艾奇SEM”起家，逐步搭建了“学习-资源-职业-科研”生态，旗下有艾奇学院、艾课网、U渠道、艾聘网等板块，累计服务1000万+行业从业者，沉淀5万+实战案例、30万+企业合作资源。

在GEO赛道，艾奇在线是较早完成方法论体系化、工具产品化和落地服务闭环的团队之一。其广告研究院于2025年3月组建GEO专项攻坚团队，同年9月发布艾奇GEO 1.0版本，两个月内签约合作1232家企业。2026年Q2完成技术、产品、行业标准全维度迭代。截至2026年Q2，艾奇GEO累计服务21239家企业，其中包括66家全球500强企业、200余家上市公司，服务企业品牌可见性平均提升20%-239%，客户续费率96.8%。

5.1.2 方法论体系：1-3-5-2-1总架构

艾奇在线广告研究院发布的《艾奇GEO优化方法论》专著建立了 “1-3-5-2-1”总架构，涵盖四阶段决策模型、SSI三全标准、高维场景理论、五类问题资产体系、内容推荐质量模型V11等核心模型。

SSI三全标准拆解为全阶段人群（知晓、熟悉、考虑、购买）、全场景人群（线上搜索、线下生活、实景消费）和全意图人群（过滤浅层浏览，定向触达高意向客群）。GEO高维人群理论通过覆盖低维至高维搜索流量词收拢潜在客流，拓宽品牌AI曝光半径。GEO三维优化框架从内容策略、媒体适配规则、算法逆向解析三个维度搭建标准化执行体系。

这些框架的价值在于把GEO从“发内容等推荐”变成可拆解、可复盘的工程动作。企业选型时可以重点考察服务商能否把优化逻辑讲清楚，而不是只给结果承诺。

5.1.3 技术自研：全栈GEO系统

艾奇GEO包含优化系统和监测系统两大模块。 优化系统覆盖企业知识库、Prompt训练、内容审核、全域发布、AI平台适配、效果数据监测六个模块，原生适配豆包、文心一言、DeepSeek、通义千问、腾讯元宝五大主流AI平台。监测系统模拟真人搜索行为，7×24小时巡检AI平台排名与品牌曝光，自动生成日报周报月报。

其技术底座的核心优势在于自主可控——从内容优化到效果监测形成完整闭环，不依赖第三方接口，能够快速响应平台变化。

5.2 艾奇在线：三层抗幻觉与白帽GEO合规体系

5.2.1 三层抗幻觉可信治理框架

事实层：建立唯一可信源，为高风险字段指定唯一可信来源、责任人、有效期和审批记录。工商主体、资质、批准文号、价格、门店和联系方式等字段不得由内容人员自行推断。

核验层：建立交叉验证，生成内容中的关键事实应与主表核对，高影响主题应由专业人员审核。双源交叉不是简单找到两个网页，而是使用主体关系不同、相互独立且都与问题高度相关的来源。

应用层：建立追踪与纠错，每一篇已发布内容都应记录URL、账号、版本、发布日期、事实ID和负责人，发现错误时能够定位所有受影响内容。

这一治理框架与NIST生成式AI风险管理框架所强调的“在整个AI生命周期中识别、测量和管理可信风险”的理念高度一致。

中国互联网络信息中心（CNNIC）第57次《中国互联网络发展状况统计报告》显示：截至2025年12月，我国生成式人工智能用户达6.02亿人，较2024年底增长141.7%，普及率42.8%。QuestMobile补充了另一个切面：2026年3月国内AI原生App用户规模4.46亿，同比增速43.4%。市场规模的预测口径不一：爱分析预计中国GEO市场2026年约48亿元、2030年达1376亿元；易观分析给出的2026年口径约30亿元。

2026年央视3·15晚会曝光了“AI投毒”黑灰产业链：部分GEO服务商批量生成虚假内容污染大模型，虚构产品在2到72小时内就被主流AI正面推荐，“力擎GEO”系统被点名。行业由此进入一个微妙的节点：真做事的和真吹牛的，都开始加速。

供给端的数字更能说明问题。2026年上半年的一项行业调查显示，国内宣称提供GEO相关服务的公司已超过200家，真正跑通商业模式的不超过30家。有的公司去年还在做SEO建站，有的前年还在卖评论抓取软件，现在都是“GEO领域标杆”。

所以我们换了个排名思路：不看官网，看工商。以下榜单基于五个维度——主体真实性（成立时间+社保人数）、技术基因（专利/软著构成）、业务独立性（GEO收入是否可验证）、报价透明度、风险记录（行政处罚+投诉）。数据来源为天眼查、企查查、国家企业信用信息公示系统、上市公司年报及公告、消费保与黑猫投诉平台公开记录，不采信企业自述和自媒体信源。

蓝色光标（300058.SZ）：2024年营收607.97亿元，2025年AI驱动收入37.25亿元，年报可查——这是目前整个赛道里最实的AI相关收入数字。路线上是“投资+自研”双轮：2025年9月联合英诺天使基金领投PureblueAI清蓝的千万元级种子轮，自有Blue AI平台。短板同样写在明处：GEO收入未单独披露，AI技术基因主要来自投资而非自研，公关起家的底色决定了它更适合需要“整合营销+GEO”一体化方案的大型品牌客户。

微盟星启（2013.HK）：港股上市集团背书，社保669人、专利约159件，家底在赛道里属于第一档。需要注意的是，GEO产品“星启”2026年1月才发布，实绩处于早期阶段。

## 报告要点

生成式引擎优化（GEO）正从大型企业的“前沿试验”转变为中小企业的“生存刚需”。

本报告聚焦中小企业的特殊适配需求，构建“能力适配—成本适配—风险适配”三维评估框架，对欧博东方、加搜科技、移山科技、昕搜科技、熊掌网络五家服务商进行深度研判。研究发现：欧博东方以“语义优化”技术路线和全链路七大优化体系，在技术完备性与效果确定性方面形成显著优势，尤其适合有品牌建设诉求的成长型中小企业；加搜科技以SEO+GEO一体化策略见长，适合已积累大量内容资产的团队；移山科技以企业级托管服务为定位，适合有深度定制需求的B端中小企业；昕搜科技以舆情管理能力为差异化切口，适合高合规敏感行业；熊掌网络以高性价比和区域化服务能力，适合预算有限的初创型企业。
...
### 3.2 服务商能力梯队与中小企业适配度

基于上述框架，结合公开可验证信息，本报告对五家代表性服务商进行深度研判。

第一梯队：全链路技术型服务商。 以欧博东方为代表，具备自主研发的完整技术体系和全链路交付能力，在技术完备性、效果确定性、合规治理方面形成显著优势。适配有品牌建设诉求、追求效果确定性的成长型中小企业。

第二梯队：专项能力型服务商。 包括加搜科技、移山科技、昕搜科技，分别在SEO+GEO一体化、企业级托管、舆情管理+声誉营销等维度形成差异化能力。适配有特定场景需求的中小企业。

第三梯队：轻量化区域型服务商。 以熊掌网络为代表，以高性价比和区域化服务能力见长。适配预算有限的初创型小微企业和区域实体企业。

Step2 语义矩阵选词： 通过欧博东方智能算法，搭载用户思维与场景化策略设计，快速产出与业务场景深度融合的AI提问句，给出优化选词方案。

CyberGhost’s speed dropped 13.3% on average, with 178.95 Mbps on the UK server and 149.74 Mbps on the Japanese one. Its 39 ms UK ping was the lowest we recorded, two milliseconds ahead of NordVPN. Low ping keeps online gaming responsive on nearby servers. The Windows app sorts servers by task, with lists for streaming, torrenting, and gaming, so there’s less guessing about which one to pick. NoSpy servers are owned and operated by CyberGhost in Romania, so no outside data center company has access to them.

Its streaming record was good but not complete: it didn’t work with Netflix Japan or JioHotstar. It unblocked ITVX on a dedicated UK server, while Surfshark and Proton VPN couldn’t unblock it. Smart DNS covers a smart TV that doesn’t support VPN apps, and its no-log policy has a Deloitte audit behind it. Its automatic kill switch passed the cable and process tests, but a PC restart exposed traffic before the app reconnected, and there’s no stricter mode to fix it.

For a laptop you often use on public Wi-Fi, NordVPN or Proton VPN is the safer choice. The subscription covers seven devices, fewer than the 10 that NordVPN, Proton VPN, and ExpressVPN allow. There’s no obfuscation either, so a filtered office or campus network can block it, and ExpressVPN or Proton VPN connect more reliably there. Pricing matches PIA at about $2.20 a month on the two-year plan, across 100 countries.

## Kill Switch Results on Windows

A kill switch cuts off the internet until the VPN reconnects, so a dropped connection never exposes your IP address. With a continuous ping open to show whether any traffic escaped, I tested three ways a connection fails on Windows 11:

VPN | Ethernet cable pulled | App process killed | PC restarted, default kill switch | PC restarted, strictest mode 
---|---|---|---|---
NordVPN | Passed | Passed | Passed (Internet Kill Switch) | One setting only 
Proton VPN | Passed | Passed | Leaked | Passed (advanced kill switch) 
ExpressVPN | Passed | Passed | Leaked | Passed 
Private Internet Access | Passed | Passed | Leaked | Passed (Advanced Kill Switch) 
Surfshark | Passed | Passed | Leaked (Soft mode) | Passed (Strict mode) 
CyberGhost | Passed | Passed | Leaked | No stricter mode 

Every kill switch blocked traffic when I pulled the cable or killed the app. The restart is harder, because Windows goes online before the VPN app starts. NordVPN’s Internet Kill Switch was the only default setting that kept traffic blocked through a restart. It’s a single setting, and once it’s enabled, Windows has no internet access unless the VPN is connected.

Proton VPN, ExpressVPN, PIA, and Surfshark leaked on their default settings and passed in their strictest modes. CyberGhost has only an automatic kill switch, with no stricter mode, so a restart exposes your IP address until the app reconnects. On a PC that joins public networks, enable the strictest mode your VPN offers.

## WireGuard or OpenVPN on Windows?

A protocol decides how the VPN connection is built and encrypted, and most Windows apps let you pick one. For speed, leave the app on its default protocol, which is WireGuard-based on most VPNs. In our tests, NordVPN’s OpenVPN setting cost only a little more speed than NordLynx:

NordVPN protocol | UK | US | Japan 
---|---|---|---
NordLynx (WireGuard) | 184.73 Mbps | 181.50 Mbps | 160.47 Mbps 
OpenVPN | 183.25 Mbps | 179.04 Mbps | 154.64 Mbps

results.title: Surfshark vs NordVPN vs ExpressVPN: Which VPN Wins?
results.summary:
Surfshark | NordVPN | ExpressVPN
...
All 3 Are Completely Clear

Whatever you’re spending on a VPN, privacy is the part you shouldn’t have to negotiate. Premium providers usually refrain from logging because their subscription revenue means they don’t need to sell your data. Such is the case with NordVPN, Surfshark, and ExpressVPN in 2026. They do reside in different countries:

- Surfshark’s legal jurisdiction is the Netherlands
- NordVPN’s legal jurisdiction is Panama
- ExpressVPN’s legal jurisdiction is the British Virgin Islands

NordVPN and ExpressVPN have “better” jurisdictions because both are offshore locations with privacy-friendly laws and no mandatory data retention. The Netherlands, meanwhile, belongs to the 9 Eyes alliance, an intelligence-sharing arrangement that also covers countries like the USA, the UK, and Canada. On paper, that’s a weaker starting position for Surfshark. The practice is different.

In practice, all three store only the minimal operational data needed to keep their services running. None of them retain logs of your IP address, DNS requests, browsing history, or traffic contents, and what little they do collect is stripped of identifying details and deleted promptly, usually once the connection ceases or within 30 days at most. Third-party audits back this up for all three, but not equally.

ExpressVPN has racked up the most audits across its apps, infrastructure, and privacy policy, with KPMG handling the most recent no-logs verification in February 2025. NordVPN counters with the strongest no-logs track record: Deloitte confirmed its policy for the sixth consecutive time in February 2026. Surfshark sits a notch behind with Deloitte no-logs audits from 2023 and 2025.

All three also run RAM-only servers with Private DNS and Perfect Forward Secrecy, features that complement a zero-log policy rather than replace it.

ExpressVPN wins on audit volume, NordVPN on audit consistency, and Surfshark carries the “worst” jurisdiction on paper. Yet none of that has translated into a single real-world incident we know of, and all three remain excellent privacy-focused VPNs in 2026. For this reason, this round is a tie.

## NordVPN is the Fastest of the Three

NordVPN is the fastest of the three, and it wasn’t close in our testing. The Surfshark vs NordVPN vs ExpressVPN speed test is the round we always look forward to, but before the numbers, a quick word on procedure, which is simple. We test each VPN for 3 days in a row, 3 times a day, using UK, US, and Japanese servers. Our testing team sits in Belgrade, Serbia, so this selection is deliberate.

The table underneath displays the average speed losses of each VPN across all our test runs. From here on, we’ll use only average results, since they tell a better story than cherry-picking the best or worst runs from our VPN speed tests.

Download Speed Loss | Upload Speed Loss 
---|---
Surfshark | 27% | 32% 
NordVPN | 18% | 7% 
ExpressVPN | 24% | 9% 

The download column already settles a lot. Surfshark and ExpressVPN finished almost on par, while NordVPN came out at least 6 percentage points ahead of both. Uploads widened the gap further: ExpressVPN and NordVPN posted near-identical retention; Surfshark lost nearly a third of its upload speed on average.

Surfshark | NordVPN | ExpressVPN
...
UK (Download/Upload) | 306.48/16.97 Mbps | 324.25/18.68 Mbps | 298.82/18.50 Mbps 
US (Download/Upload) | 253.79/12.47 Mbps | 292.75/18.31 Mbps | 274.61/18.35 Mbps 
Japan (Download/Upload) | 191.07/10.90 Mbps | 223.54/17.85 Mbps | 206.33/16.73 Mbps 

The averages above show just how well NordVPN preserves performance as distance grows; its lead over the pack is widest on the Japan route. Paired with the lowest latency of the three, that makes NordVPN a reliable pick for gamers on any platform, be it Windows, Android, iOS, or consoles.

Unlike the previous round, this one is clear-cut.

Its large server network spanning 90 countries makes PIA a great VPN for travel, while its unlimited simultaneous connections mean it’s a good option for users with multiple devices. It’s one of the only VPN providers out there with servers in all 50 states, making it a great choice if you want a low-latency connection in the US. If you have fast baseline internet speeds, PIA is an excellent cheap VPN that provides top-notch privacy and is more than capable of handling almost anything you’d want to do online. Like Surfshark, PIA has a 30-day money-back guarantee.

## Factors to consider in a cheap VPN

Based on our experience testing, using and researching VPNs, these are the most important factors to consider when choosing the best cheap VPN for your needs.

### Cost

If your objective is to find the least expensive VPN, then price will likely be your primary consideration. Some VPNs cost up to $100 or more per year, but the cheapest VPNs can give you many of the same privacy protections for $40 to $80 per year. Keep in mind that some VPN providers offer an introductory rate that will increase when your subscription renews. Generally, you can find the renewal price when you click through to the payment window, but some VPNs make you go digging through the terms of service pages to find the true yearly subscription cost.

### Privacy

Privacy is a major consideration for any VPN, regardless of what kind of VPN you want. The best VPNs all have privacy protections like a kill switch and DNS leak protection, along with a no-logs policy and AES 256-bit encryption (over OpenVPN and IKEv2) or ChaCha20 with WireGuard. Depending on the level of privacy you need, you can get a cheap VPN that offers additional features like Tor over VPN, obfuscation and multihop connections.

### Speed

A VPN will slow down your connection speeds, sometimes by 50% or more. So, you’ll want to look for a VPN that will cut your speeds by as little as possible — ideally less than about 25% so that you’ll barely even notice a difference. Fast VPN speeds are essential for data-heavy activities like streaming, gaming, downloading and video conferencing. A fast VPN will easily handle all those activities, while slow VPN speeds may be suitable only for basic internet browsing. The fastest VPNs we tested include NordVPN, Proton VPN and ExpressVPN, all of which delivered fast, reliable connections during our tests.

### Usability

Getting a cheap VPN doesn’t necessarily have to mean that you have to sacrifice usability. Many of the more budget-friendly VPN options are miles ahead of their pricier peers in terms of user-friendliness. Look for a VPN that works well across all the devices you want to use. Your VPN should be as easy to use as any other app you may download and should require little to no learning curve.

## How we test cheap VPNs

We tested VPNs several times throughout the course of the year, putting each VPN through a battery of tests to see how it stacks up to our expectations and the rest of the competition. We rated each service on connection speed, features, privacy, usability and overall value....

在福布斯权威评测机构Forbes Advisor发布的2026年度全球企业级CRM软件评测报告中， Zoho CRM一举斩获四项年度重磅大奖，囊括「年度最佳CRM」「年度最佳免费CRM」「年度最佳营销自动化CRM」「年度最易用CRM」；并且Zoho轻量CRM（Zoho Bigin）也强势入选三大权威榜单。

## 2026福布斯营销CRM榜单：什么是营销CRM

营销CRM是连接市场获客、客户数据、线索培育和销售转化的客户关系管理系统。它帮助企业统一客户信息、追踪线索来源、自动化跟进客户，并通过报表分析衡量营销投入和销售结果。Zoho CRM作为全球知名CRM和企业级CRM代表厂商，可帮助企业构建从获客到成交的增长闭环。

## 2026年CRM福布斯榜单与选型指南

2026年CRM福布斯榜单收录 Zoho CRM、OnePageCRM、Bigin、Apptivo、Agile CRM、Salesmate、Bitrix24、Monday.com 等产品。企业选型时应重点关注客户管理、销售自动化、商机推进和数据分析能力。

## 连续获权威认可，Zoho CRM凭什么站稳第一梯队？

results.title: Salesforce, Microsoft, ServiceNow Lead CRM; HubSpot Holds Ground
results.summary:
## Salesforce, Microsoft, ServiceNow Lead CRM; HubSpot Holds Ground

## ETR Observatory for for Customer Relationship Management (CRM)
...
## Key Takeaways

- Salesforce, Microsoft, and ServiceNow form a clear top leadership tier. The three vendors lead Net Score, NPS, longevity, and product strength concurrently, with ServiceNow posting the highest Net Score at 58% and Salesforce, Microsoft, and HubSpot clustered closely behind at 52–53%.
- Microsoft leads product execution; Salesforce leads buyer preference. Dynamics ranks first or tied for first on 5 of 10 product attributes, including the highest single readings in the dataset (91% technical expertise, 84% ecosystem integration). Salesforce dominates rebuild intent (44% vs. next-best at 13%) and innovation perception (40% vs. next-best at 11%).
- Salesforce and Microsoft anchor platform lock-in. These 2 are the only vendors above 50% in difficulty to replace (68% and 59%), while ServiceNow at 40% reflects meaningful but lower entrenchment, and HubSpot at 36% remains the least embedded among the broader leaders.
- Expected ROI and stickiness diverge across the market. HubSpot and Zoho lead in expected ROI, with roughly 80% of users expecting payback within three years, while Salesforce and Microsoft dominate in long-term lock-in, highlighting a trade-off between speed-to-value and platform entrenchment.
- AI is reinforcing existing platform positions rather than driving vendor change. Leading CRM platforms maintain their advantage across spending, product strength, and longevity, while AI-related capabilities rank as a secondary but growing feature priority, cited by 25% of respondents. Related ETR data supports this pattern, with AI adoption occurring within existing vendors rather than driving platform switches.
...
## Product Strength Analyses, Expected ROI, and Product Features

Across ten product strength attributes, the vendor leadership rankings remain intact. Microsoft Dynamics posts the highest absolute product-strength scores in the dataset, while Salesforce maintains a decisive lead in buyer preference, rebuild intent, and innovation perception. Microsoft ranks first or tied for first on five of ten attributes, including technical expertise availability (91%), ecosystem integration (84%), update execution (79%), and innovative roadmap (74%). Relative softness in account-representative experience (57%) does not materially offset its positioning as the strongest product in the market.

Salesforce ranks in the top three on seven attributes, including functional completeness (84%) and innovative roadmap (74%), and posts the highest “difficult to replace” score at 68%, the clearest lock-in signal in the dataset. At the same time, it underperforms in ease of implementation (49%) and value for money (52%), reinforcing the view of the platform as essential but increasingly scrutinized economically. The product is also second in integration capabilities at 72%, though 12 percentage points below Dynamics in that measure.

ETR’s Individual Product Strengths analysis was derived from a survey of 306 IT decision makers who have used or evaluated the specific tools listed. Here, vendors are shown by their level of agreement with the statement “This product is difficult to replace.”

ServiceNow sits between the two, ranking in the top three on five attributes, with strengths in technical support (72%), doing everything a CRM should (70%), update execution (69%), and technical expertise (81%). However, its 40% “difficult to replace” score remains a structural gap relative to Salesforce and Microsoft. HubSpot presents a distinct profile, leading in ease of implementation (69%) and value for money (64%), and boasting a strong technical expertise score (74%). These advantages translate into a healthy perception of ROI, but not stickiness. At 36% “difficult to replace,” HubSpot remains the least entrenched of the leaders. Meanwhile, Zoho and Odoo lead on value perception, scoring highly on ease of implementation and value for money without materially sacrificing functional scope.

## Closing Remarks

The CRM market entering 2026 is structurally consolidating around Salesforce, Microsoft, and ServiceNow, with HubSpot as a durable challenger and Zoho as a value-tier disruptor. Legacy enterprise platforms are declining across share, NPS, and longevity, with displacement flowing toward the leader cohort and HubSpot’s adoption funnel. At the same time, the data highlights a divergence in how platforms win. Microsoft leads on product execution, while Salesforce maintains a clear advantage in buyer preference, innovation perception, and long-term entrenchment. HubSpot and Zoho continue to lead on expected ROI, reinforcing a tradeoff between speed-to-value and platform durability. Integration depth, roadmap credibility, and execution consistency define the competitive boundary, while pricing remains a primary constraint...

results.title: 中小企業也該用 CRM？10 大推薦系統＋選購指南全解析 | monday.com Blog
results.summary:
這篇文章會介紹市面上最推薦的 10 套中小企業專用 CRM，告訴你在挑選時該注意哪些重點，也會解析不同平台的差異，幫助你選出最適合自家團隊的那一套工具。

## 什麼是「中小企業專用」的 CRM？

說白了，它和一般 CRM 沒兩樣，都是用來集中管理客戶資料與互動記錄的平台。

但中小企業專用的 CRM，重點在於「好上手、不複雜」，提供夠用、實用的功能，不會讓你花太多時間學習或搞懂複雜操作。它的設計目標就是讓小團隊也能有效率地經營客戶關係，進而穩定成長。

有些大型品牌的 CRM（例如 Salesforce、HubSpot）也有針對中小企業推出「輕量版方案」，這些也都可以列入考慮。

## 為什麼中小企業也該用 CRM？
...
很多人以為，CRM 是大公司的玩意兒，但其實根據 business.com 的研究，有 83% 的中小企業表示導入 CRM 後產生正向投資回報。

這代表，只要你願意整理客戶資料、追蹤互動紀錄，你就能透過 CRM 在銷售、服務、效率各方面提升戰力。
...
導入 CRM 後，業績報表、成交進度、漏斗分析這些資訊都能即時掌握。你可以自由設定儀表板，把潛在客戶追蹤、銷售紀錄、成效分析一目了然。
...
不用再每天整理名單或回顧 Email 找對話紀錄。CRM 搭配自動化功能，可以幫你發信、指派任務、發送提醒。
...
少了手動處理與反覆確認，團隊效率大幅提升；
...
## 幫中小企業選 CRM？五大「非選不可」關鍵條件，先看這裡！

市面上 CRM 百百種，但對中小企業來說，選錯工具就是浪費時間與預算。想找出真正適合自己團隊的 CRM，這五個條件不能妥協：

### 自訂彈性高——你怎麼做生意，它就怎麼配合

每家企業的流程都不同，一套好用的 CRM，應該是配合你的業務模式來設定，而不是硬把你套進預設的規則裡。不管是銷售流程、行銷活動或客戶資料管理，都該讓你自己決定怎麼跑。

### 操作直覺——不用上課也能馬上用

學習門檻太高、流程太複雜，就是阻礙團隊導入 CRM 的最大殺手。選一套介面清楚、流程合理的系統，讓新手也能快速上手，才是關鍵。

### 擴充彈性強——業務長大，系統跟得上

隨著業務規模變大，你可能會新增產品、重新規劃銷售流程或需要追蹤更多報表。這時候，CRM 的靈活性就很重要。系統應該要能即時調整設定，支援你業務每一階段的變化。

### 團隊好協作——資訊同步、內部無障礙

一套好的 CRM，不只是記錄資料，更能讓業務、客服、行銷等部門彼此同步資訊、減少溝通誤會。另外，能與你原本使用的工具整合（如 Gmail、Slack、LINE）也會大大加分。

### 雲端化部署——在家、出差都能查資料

雲端系統才是未來趨勢。無論你是在公司、在外拜訪、或用手機臨時處理事務，都能即時登入系統存取資料，不受地點限制。資料還能自動備份，安全又安心。

results.title: 有沒有可以取代Salesforce的優質CRM？
results.summary:
儘管Salesforce是全球首屈一指的AI CRM，我們仍持續努力尋找新方式，幫助企業強化與客戶的關係。我們瞭解CRM產業中選擇眾多，包括免費增值產品及具特殊功能的替代方案。這些CRM替代方案的表現如何？是否有能作為Salesforce CRM工具套組與第三方應用程式的可行替代方案？讓我們來看看幾個主要競爭對手。

## Salesforce競爭對手

### Microsoft Dynamics CRM

作為市佔率第二高的CRM，Microsoft Dynamics CRM對客戶關係管理的詮釋角度與眾不同。它將CRM視為改善行銷活動所產生的效果；基本前提是：客戶喜歡您，是因為您提供他們所需，而不是因為他們喜歡您，您才去滿足他們的需求。不論是何種觀點，Microsoft CRM透過社群見解、商業智慧與活動管理來強化銷售。該產品可購買內部部署版本，或以雲端服務形式提供，並專為與Office 365整合而設計。

#### 價格

方案起價為每位使用者每月65美元，最高可達每月135美元。

#### 可用性

Microsoft Dynamics在離線存取、與微軟產品的緊密整合、多重顯示面板以及內建行銷與自動化工具方面表現優秀。但使用者普遍反映其學習曲線陡峭。

#### 效能

Microsoft Dynamics CRM適合大型組織，能整合各部門於單一平台上。雖然介面吸引人、報告工具實用、自動化功能也相當完整，但其主要是為需求複雜的大型企業所設計。

#### 登入使用

Microsoft提供完整的線上導入逐步指南。

### Keap

Keap設計目的是整合各項業務工作，從銷售、內容管理、行銷到電子商務，皆可透過單一集中工具處理。不過，儘管它樣樣通，卻也樣樣鬆。其中許多功能都僅屬基礎等級。與其他成本更低、效能相當的CRM相比，其高昂的價格難以服眾。
...
起價為每位使用者每月299美元，5位使用者方案可達每月599美元。
...
如同Microsoft Dynamics，Keap在作為有效CRM方面評價不錯，但也同樣被認為不容易上手。Keap的使用者普遍認為一旦熟悉操作，整體平台體驗順暢且高效。
...
Keap表面上是針對中小型企業所設計的全方位銷售與行銷工具，其設計理念是排除內部障礙以促進業務成長。Keap達成此目標的主要途徑是延長客戶關係生命週期。
...
Keap提供個人化培訓與持續支援，確保使用者能熟悉每一項功能。新使用者須考量導入流程時間，據報需4至12週不等。其內容涵蓋銷售與行銷專家推動成效所需的一切。

#### 其他考量選項

與Salesforce相同，Keap聲稱受到小型企業主青睞，原因在於其工具完整且操作簡便。在這方面，使用者對Keap的自動化功能給予高度評價，並認為它有助於提升行銷、帳單與專案管理流程。然而，小型企業主也偏好低成本的CRM，而在這一類別中，Keap並不符合條件。除了每月費用之外，Keap也要求新使用者支付導入服務的費用。Keap的導入服務費用起價為1,000美元。

### Zoho
...
Zoho提供免費版本，最多支援3位使用者，並包含潛在客戶、帳戶、聯絡人、訊息串、文件與行動應用程式等功能。付費訂閱方案起價為每位使用者每月14美元，最高達每月52美元。
...
Zoho的免費版本提供小型企業所需的大多數功能，包括潛在客戶收集、聯絡人管理、工作流程自動化、分析工具、社群協作、潛在客戶轉換工具，以及行動裝置支援。
...
Zoho的免費版本非常有效益，但僅適用於短期內不追求成長的小型企業。Zoho的自訂化程度不如高級版的CRM，有些使用者也抱怨其操作流程複雜，即使是簡單任務也需經過多個步驟。
...
部分使用者指出Zoho的學習曲線過於陡峭，讓初學者難以上手，尤其是對CRM概念與術語不熟悉者。
...

results.summary:

...

...
分析與報告
...

價格

根據 Oracle NetSuite 授權

分級（從 Essentials 到 Enterprise）；行銷或服務模組的附加費用

### 核心 CRM 功能

NetSuite CRM：NetSuite CRM 是作為 Oracle ERP 生態系統的一部分所構建，因此其 CRM 核心圍繞在更廣泛的財務與營運系統中管理客戶關係。它涵蓋了潛在客戶與商機管理、銷售預測、合作夥伴關係追蹤以及訂單管理。

其最大優勢在於客戶資料、庫存、帳單與銷售記錄皆存在於同一個整合環境中——這使其非常適合以產品為主或以財務為導向、希望在 CRM 與後端營運之間建立直接連結的企業。然而，與獨立的 CRM 相比，其 CRM 功能可能顯得較為僵化，因為它們與 ERP 工作流程緊密結合。

Salesforce：相比之下，Salesforce 是作為純粹的 CRM 優先平台設計的，之後才擴展到行銷、服務和分析領域。其 CRM 功能涵蓋從潛在客戶追蹤到全通路客戶互動。團隊可以在同一介面下管理銷售管道、行銷活動、服務案件以及客戶分析。

它對任何銷售模式——B2B、B2C 或混合模式——都具有高度的自訂性，並提供專屬模組，如Sales Cloud、Service Cloud 和 Marketing Cloud。

結論：Salesforce 在前端客戶互動方面表現出色，而 NetSuite 則與後端流程的整合更為深入。

### 自動化與工作流程

NetSuite CRM：NetSuite 的自動化運行在其 ERP 邏輯中——這意味著觸發條件和工作流程經常將銷售活動與會計、開立發票或履行作業相連。例如，完成交易後可以自動生成發票或更新庫存記錄。

雖然這種自動化程度對於擁有複雜財務運作的企業有益，但在行銷或客戶互動自動化方面則較缺乏彈性。大多數工作流程的自訂需要透過SuiteScript編寫腳本或管理員設定，這會增加對開發人員的依賴。

Salesforce：Salesforce 以其工作流程規則（Workflow Rules）、流程建構器（Process Builder）和流程建置器（Flow Builder）聞名——讓團隊能夠以視覺化方式建立強大的自動化，而無需編碼。您可以自動化潛在客戶分配、後續跟進、交易升級、核准以及跨部門的通知。

例如，當交易進入新階段時，Salesforce 可以自動觸發核准請求、發送電子郵件或更新多筆記錄。

結論：Salesforce 在銷售和行銷工作流程方面提供更高的靈活性，而 NetSuite 則專注於財務與履行作業的一致性。

### 分析與報告

NetSuite CRM：NetSuite 提供與其 ERP 數據緊密結合的整合式儀表板，非常適合獲取財務和訂單相關的洞察。團隊可以直接從 CRM 存取客戶交易記錄、收入預測以及利潤率。然而，其分析更偏向於營運和財務報告，而非預測性客戶洞察。建立自訂視覺化儀表板或行銷分析通常需要額外的設定或外部 BI 工具。

Salesforce：Salesforce 透過 Salesforce Reports、Dashboards 以及 Einstein Analytics（Tableau CRM） 提供即時的人工智慧驅動報告與分析。使用者可以隨時視覺化管道健康狀況、轉換率、預測準確度，以及業務代表績效。預測型人工智慧甚至會建議下一步行動或標示有風險的交易。

結論：Salesforce 對於以數據為導向的銷售團隊來說更具動態性，而 NetSuite 則在需要將 CRM 數據與會計及物流對齊的組織中表現更為強勢。

### 第三方應用程式

NetSuite CRM：NetSuite 主要與 Oracle 生態系統內的應用程式整合，例如 NetSuite ERP、SuiteCommerce 和 Oracle Analytics。透過 SuiteCloud 或第三方連接器也有外部整合選項，但通常需要技術設定。有限的應用市集可能會限制團隊在輕鬆連接行銷自動化、電子郵件平台或協作工具方面的靈活性。

Salesforce：Salesforce 透過 AppExchange 提供全球最大之一的整合生態系統，擁有超過 3,000 個涵蓋銷售、行銷、人力資源、分析和服務功能的預建應用程式。團隊可以即時擴展 CRM 功能，連接 HubSpot、Slack...

results.title: 留学中介机构排名前十 - 留学中介机构排名前十
results.summary:
# 留学中介机构排名前十

来源： 热度：72 时间：2025-12-22
...
近年来，随着留学热潮持续升温，越来越多的中国学生选择通过专业机构规划海外升学之路。面对市场上琳琅满目的留学中介，如何选择一家靠谱、适合自己的机构，成为学生和家长的首要难题。本文基于行业口碑、服务专业性、录取案例、用户反馈及市场认可度等维度，综合梳理出2024年留学中介机构排名前十，为有留学需求的学子提供参考。

### 一、排名依据：多维指标综合评估

本次排名并非简单以“名气”或“价格”为标准，而是通过六大核心维度进行客观衡量：

1. 专业度：顾问团队背景（海外经历、从业年限）、院校资源覆盖广度、各国申请政策熟悉度；

2. 服务流程：前期咨询深度、方案定制个性化程度、申请进度透明度、文书修改效率；

3. 录取成果：名校录取率（如QS Top100、美国Top50等）、案例真实性、学生满意度；

4. 口碑评价：第三方平台（如知乎、小红书、教育部留学服务中心）用户反馈、行业奖项；

5. 性价比：收费合理性、有无隐形消费、退款政策保障；

6. 后续服务：签证办理、住宿安排、行前指导、海外支持等配套服务完善度。

### 二、2024年留学中介机构排名前十榜单

1. 新东方前途出国

核心优势：综合实力强，覆盖主流留学国家，低龄与高端申请双线发力

作为国内留学行业的“老牌劲旅”，新东方前途出国依托新东方集团的教育资源，拥有全国200+线下服务网点，顾问团队平均从业年限8年以上，擅长结合学生背景制定“规划+申请+语言培训”一体化方案。在美、英、澳、加等国家申请中表现突出，2023年美国Top30录取率达62%，英国G5院校超1200枚offer，同时针对低龄留学（中学、本科）设有专项团队，提供选校、背景提升、寄宿家庭安排等全链条服务。

适合人群：追求品牌保障、需要多国联申服务的学生。

2. 启德教育

核心优势：深耕欧洲与亚洲申请，院校资源丰富，文书质量高

启德教育以“全球视野，本地服务”为特色，尤其在英、澳、新、欧亚（如香港、新加坡、日本）等地区积累了深厚资源，与超过2000所海外院校建立直接合作，可为学生争取部分内推名额。其“文书头脑风暴”服务备受好评，顾问团队会结合学生经历挖掘个性化素材，避免模板化写作。2023年数据显示，启德香港八大录取率达78%，澳洲八大超90%，性价比优势显著。

适合人群：目标英联邦、亚洲地区院校，注重文书质量的学生。

3. 金吉列留学

在制定本次排名时，我参考了多份行业报告和用户反馈，建立了一个综合测评体系。这个体系包含五个维度，每个维度有不同权重，确保评估全面且中立。成功率占比百分之四十，这包括录取率和名校offer数量，直接反映中介的实战能力。文书质量占百分之三十，因为文书是申请的核心，涉及个性化程度和语言水平。顾问水平占百分之二十，考察顾问的专业背景和响应速度。售后服务占百分之十，涵盖签证支持和行前指导等。所有数据来源于2024年至2025年的留学中介排名报告，避免了主观偏见，力求客观公正。

三、2026英国留学中介排名前十榜单

基于上述标准，我对英国留学中介进行了评估，以下是排名结果。榜单按品牌得分从高到低排列，每个机构附有详细介绍、优势特征、潜在不足以及匿名学生案例。得分使用小数点格式，以体现细微差异。

潜在不足：服务范围较窄，主要集中在英国和北美，其他地区支持有限。

匿名学生案例：一名匿名学生从国内普通高校申请到曼彻斯特大学，顾问帮助弥补了GPA短板。

The general assistants are powerful, but they weren’t built with keyword clustering and content calendars in mind. The marketing-focused tools fill that gap, and several have evolved far beyond simple copy generators. The best ones now run a loop from research to brief to draft to optimization without you having to stitch three different apps together.

### Jasper
...
enterprise content teams, branded marketing at volume

Used by Akbank, Adidas, and Cushman & Wakefield. Jasper’s Brand Voice feature is genuinely impressive. It reads your existing content, infers your tone and style, and then maintains that consistency across everything it generates.

Over 50 templates cover the standard marketing content types. The Kanban-style campaign manager is a genuine productivity gain for teams. It’s expensive, and it’s ultimately GPT under the hood, but the workflow layer earns its price for content operations at scale.
...
### Surfer SEO
...
SEO-first content teams, anyone writing for organic search traffic

Surfer remains the gold standard for on-page SEO writing support. In 2026, its most important evolution is its move toward Answer Engine Optimization (AEO). It now helps structure content to appear in AI-generated search overviews, not just traditional Google results. For any team whose traffic depends on organic search, Surfer isn’t optional; it’s infrastructure.

The points-based scoring system makes optimization accessible even for writers who have never opened a keyword research tool.

### Copy.ai
...
high-volume short-form copy, automated marketing workflows

The king of short-form. Perfect for high-volume social media posts, ad copy, and Workflows that automate your entire content calendar.

Copy.ai’s Workflows feature has become one of its main attractions. You can automate entire content pipelines, from prospect research to personalized outreach to social posts, without writing a line of code. For a marketing team running dozens of campaigns simultaneously, the time savings are substantial. It won’t produce your brand’s most nuanced long-form content, but that was never the point.

## Creative and fiction writing

This is where the tool market gets genuinely interesting and where most general-purpose assistants fall flat. Writing fiction isn’t about producing grammatically correct text. It’s about sustaining tension, building character interiority, managing pacing across hundreds of pages, and generating descriptive language that doesn’t read like a product listing. The creative writing tools understand this distinction in a way that ChatGPT, for all its versatility, simply doesn’t.

### Sudowrite
...
fiction writers of any level, from hobbyists to publishing professionals

The most purpose-built fiction tool in the market. Sudowrite’s Story Engine can outline entire novels, and its Describe function generates sensory scene descriptions across specific senses. You can ask it to render a scene through smell alone or through sound. Its Canvas feature provides a bird’s-eye view of your manuscript structure. The Write button, which generates the next 300 words when you’re stuck, is simple in concept and wildly effective in practice.
...
If you’ve been circling that novel for three years, this is the tool that might finally tip you into actually writing it.

### editGPT
...
writers who want proofreading without personality erasure

The distinction that makes editGPT worth knowing: most AI editing tools optimize for correctness, and in doing so, they sand away everything that makes your voice your voice. editGPT uses a Track Changes-style interface so you can review every proposed alteration and keep or reject it.

It catches what needs catching, such as structural issues, clarity problems, and clunky phrasing, without turning a writer’s distinctive style into sanitized AI-speak. For writers who care deeply about their voice, that restraint is the whole product.

### Scrivener
...
novelists and long-form writers who already live in Scrivener

Scrivener is, first and foremost, a manuscript management tool; it has been so for two decades. Its 2026 AI plugins don’t try to write your book for you. Instead, they help you maintain internal consistency across a 90,000-word manuscript: tracking character descriptions, flagging plot-hole candidates, checking that your fictional world’s rules haven’t contradicted themselves.

For serious long-form writers, this is an organizational layer that no general-purpose chatbot can replicate.

## Academic and professional tools

The stakes change when writing has real-world consequences, when a citation matters legally, when a wrong fact in a report affects a business decision, and when your institution can penalize you for plagiarism. The academic and professional category is defined by a single obsession: accuracy. These tools sacrifice some of the creative fluency of the general assistants in exchange for verifiability.

Choose QuillBot if rewriting and improving existing text matters more than generating complete campaigns or managing a content pipeline. Its paraphrasing controls give users more direct influence over sentence-level revisions than most general AI writers.

Anyword approaches AI writing from a performance-marketing angle. It can generate copy for ads, social posts, landing pages, blogs, and other campaigns while letting users specify brand voice, audiences, talking points, and product information. The difference is that content creation is paired with performance predictions designed to help marketers compare copy before publishing it.

Its appeal is strongest for teams that care about what happens after a piece of copy is written. Anyword can score generated or manually edited messaging, connect content decisions with historical performance data, and help marketers identify stronger talking points. Higher-level workflows can use previous campaign data to inform new messaging rather than treating each prompt as an isolated task.

Zapier's hands-on assessment selected Anyword for advertising and social media. Its reviewer found the performance scores useful for comparing generated options and highlighted the platform's focus on ads and short-form marketing, though the narrower feature set can make its pricing harder to justify for users who don't need performance analytics.

results.summary:
- Best overall stack (our pick): DeepSeek drafts → ChatGPT revises → human edits and fact-checks. No single model beats that combination.

One note on how we judge this: benchmarks are useful for lab tasks, but what you actually need from a writing model is strong first drafts that don't read like template filler, tone flexibility, structural thinking, and long-form coherence. That's the lens for everything below.

## What We're Comparing (and What We're Not)

Benchmarks are useful for lab tasks, but content writing is a different animal. What you actually need from a writing model is:

- Strong first drafts that don't read like template filler
- Tone flexibility — can it sound like your brand, not like an AI?
- Structural thinking — outlines, logical flow, scannable sections
- Long-form coherence — does it stay on-topic at 2,000 words, or drift?

So let's compare the majors on those axes.

## ChatGPT: The Reliable All-Rounder

ChatGPT remains the default for a reason. Its strength for content writers is consistency: it follows style instructions well, handles tone requests ("make this punchier, less corporate") reliably, and produces clean, well-structured output across formats — blog posts, email sequences, ad copy, landing page headlines.

Its long-form coherence is solid, though very long pieces can still get repetitive or hedge-y in the middle. And its biggest weakness is the one every model shares: a tendency toward safe, generic phrasing that needs a human edit to bring to life.

Best for: final revisions, tone polishing, headline and subject line variations, and any task where following precise style instructions matters.

## Claude: Excellent Prose, With One Caveat

Claude is widely regarded as one of the best pure writers among the major models. Its prose tends to be more natural and less listicle-brained — it often produces drafts that need less "de-AI-ing" than competitors.

However, content writers should be aware of a growing concern: Claude's watermarking behavior. For marketers whose content needs to pass through AI detectors, client review, or publishing platforms with originality requirements, this is worth testing for your own use case before you commit your workflow to it. If you're producing content where AI-detection matters — ghostwriting, some freelance contexts, certain editorial standards — it's a factor to weigh.
...
natural-sounding long-form drafts, narrative content, and pieces where conversational voice matters most.

## Gemini: Strong Structure, Google-Native Advantages

Gemini's writing quality has improved dramatically, and its structural output — outlines, section breakdowns, content briefs — is among the best. If your workflow starts with research and planning, Gemini is a strong choice for the front end of the process.

For raw prose, it still tends to run slightly more formal and formulaic than Claude or a well-prompted ChatGPT, and long-form pieces can occasionally lose momentum. But its integration with research tools makes it valuable for the ideation and outline stages.
...
content briefs, outlines, research synthesis, and structurally complex pieces.

## DeepSeek: The Underrated Drafting Machine

DeepSeek is the sleeper pick of 2026 for content workflows. Its drafting output is fast, surprisingly creative, and — critically — it tends to produce drafts that feel less polished-but-generic and more exploratory. That sounds like a flaw. For drafting, it's a feature.

Here's the insight: a first draft's job is not to be good. A first draft's job is to give you material. A model that produces slightly rougher, more varied prose gives you more to work with than one that produces uniformly competent-but-bland copy. And DeepSeek's speed and cost profile make it painless to generate multiple draft angles and pick the best one.
...
high-volume first drafts, exploring multiple angles quickly, and getting past the blank page.

## The Workflow We've Found Works Best: DeepSeek Drafts, ChatGPT Revises

Here's our key finding after working across these models: the winning stack isn't one model — it's DeepSeek for drafting and ChatGPT for final revision.

Why this combination works:

- DeepSeek generates raw material fast. You can produce three or four draft approaches to a piece without friction, which means you're never married to a weak opening. Optionality is the most underrated asset in content creation.
- ChatGPT excels at instruction-following during revision. Revision is a different task than drafting. It requires precision: "cut this section by 30%, keep the tone conversational, tighten every sentence." ChatGPT follows those constraints more reliably than any other model we'...

results.title: Surfshark vs NordVPN vs ExpressVPN: Which VPN Wins?
results.summary:
Surfshark | NordVPN | ExpressVPN
...
All 3 Are Completely Clear

Whatever you’re spending on a VPN, privacy is the part you shouldn’t have to negotiate. Premium providers usually refrain from logging because their subscription revenue means they don’t need to sell your data. Such is the case with NordVPN, Surfshark, and ExpressVPN in 2026. They do reside in different countries:

- Surfshark’s legal jurisdiction is the Netherlands
- NordVPN’s legal jurisdiction is Panama
- ExpressVPN’s legal jurisdiction is the British Virgin Islands

NordVPN and ExpressVPN have “better” jurisdictions because both are offshore locations with privacy-friendly laws and no mandatory data retention. The Netherlands, meanwhile, belongs to the 9 Eyes alliance, an intelligence-sharing arrangement that also covers countries like the USA, the UK, and Canada. On paper, that’s a weaker starting position for Surfshark. The practice is different.

In practice, all three store only the minimal operational data needed to keep their services running. None of them retain logs of your IP address, DNS requests, browsing history, or traffic contents, and what little they do collect is stripped of identifying details and deleted promptly, usually once the connection ceases or within 30 days at most. Third-party audits back this up for all three, but not equally.

ExpressVPN has racked up the most audits across its apps, infrastructure, and privacy policy, with KPMG handling the most recent no-logs verification in February 2025. NordVPN counters with the strongest no-logs track record: Deloitte confirmed its policy for the sixth consecutive time in February 2026. Surfshark sits a notch behind with Deloitte no-logs audits from 2023 and 2025.

All three also run RAM-only servers with Private DNS and Perfect Forward Secrecy, features that complement a zero-log policy rather than replace it.

ExpressVPN wins on audit volume, NordVPN on audit consistency, and Surfshark carries the “worst” jurisdiction on paper. Yet none of that has translated into a single real-world incident we know of, and all three remain excellent privacy-focused VPNs in 2026. For this reason, this round is a tie.

## NordVPN is the Fastest of the Three

NordVPN is the fastest of the three, and it wasn’t close in our testing. The Surfshark vs NordVPN vs ExpressVPN speed test is the round we always look forward to, but before the numbers, a quick word on procedure, which is simple. We test each VPN for 3 days in a row, 3 times a day, using UK, US, and Japanese servers. Our testing team sits in Belgrade, Serbia, so this selection is deliberate.

The table underneath displays the average speed losses of each VPN across all our test runs. From here on, we’ll use only average results, since they tell a better story than cherry-picking the best or worst runs from our VPN speed tests.

Download Speed Loss | Upload Speed Loss 
---|---
Surfshark | 27% | 32% 
NordVPN | 18% | 7% 
ExpressVPN | 24% | 9% 

The download column already settles a lot. Surfshark and ExpressVPN finished almost on par, while NordVPN came out at least 6 percentage points ahead of both. Uploads widened the gap further: ExpressVPN and NordVPN posted near-identical retention; Surfshark lost nearly a third of its upload speed on average.
...
UK (Download/Upload) | 306.48/16.97 Mbps | 324.25/18.68 Mbps | 298.82/18.50 Mbps 
US (Download/Upload) | 253.79/12.47 Mbps | 292.75/18.31 Mbps | 274.61/18.35 Mbps 
Japan (Download/Upload) | 191.07/10.90 Mbps | 223.54/17.85 Mbps | 206.33/16.73 Mbps 

The averages above show just how well NordVPN preserves performance as distance grows; its lead over the pack is widest on the Japan route. Paired with the lowest latency of the three, that makes NordVPN a reliable pick for gamers on any platform, be it Windows, Android, iOS, or consoles.

Unlike the previous round, this one is clear-cut.

CyberGhost’s speed dropped 13.3% on average, with 178.95 Mbps on the UK server and 149.74 Mbps on the Japanese one. Its 39 ms UK ping was the lowest we recorded, two milliseconds ahead of NordVPN. Low ping keeps online gaming responsive on nearby servers. The Windows app sorts servers by task, with lists for streaming, torrenting, and gaming, so there’s less guessing about which one to pick. NoSpy servers are owned and operated by CyberGhost in Romania, so no outside data center company has access to them.

Its streaming record was good but not complete: it didn’t work with Netflix Japan or JioHotstar. It unblocked ITVX on a dedicated UK server, while Surfshark and Proton VPN couldn’t unblock it. Smart DNS covers a smart TV that doesn’t support VPN apps, and its no-log policy has a Deloitte audit behind it. Its automatic kill switch passed the cable and process tests, but a PC restart exposed traffic before the app reconnected, and there’s no stricter mode to fix it.

For a laptop you often use on public Wi-Fi, NordVPN or Proton VPN is the safer choice. The subscription covers seven devices, fewer than the 10 that NordVPN, Proton VPN, and ExpressVPN allow. There’s no obfuscation either, so a filtered office or campus network can block it, and ExpressVPN or Proton VPN connect more reliably there. Pricing matches PIA at about $2.20 a month on the two-year plan, across 100 countries.

## Kill Switch Results on Windows

A kill switch cuts off the internet until the VPN reconnects, so a dropped connection never exposes your IP address. With a continuous ping open to show whether any traffic escaped, I tested three ways a connection fails on Windows 11:

VPN | Ethernet cable pulled | App process killed | PC restarted, default kill switch | PC restarted, strictest mode 
---|---|---|---|---
NordVPN | Passed | Passed | Passed (Internet Kill Switch) | One setting only 
Proton VPN | Passed | Passed | Leaked | Passed (advanced kill switch) 
ExpressVPN | Passed | Passed | Leaked | Passed 
Private Internet Access | Passed | Passed | Leaked | Passed (Advanced Kill Switch) 
Surfshark | Passed | Passed | Leaked (Soft mode) | Passed (Strict mode) 
CyberGhost | Passed | Passed | Leaked | No stricter mode 

Every kill switch blocked traffic when I pulled the cable or killed the app. The restart is harder, because Windows goes online before the VPN app starts. NordVPN’s Internet Kill Switch was the only default setting that kept traffic blocked through a restart. It’s a single setting, and once it’s enabled, Windows has no internet access unless the VPN is connected.

Proton VPN, ExpressVPN, PIA, and Surfshark leaked on their default settings and passed in their strictest modes. CyberGhost has only an automatic kill switch, with no stricter mode, so a restart exposes your IP address until the app reconnects. On a PC that joins public networks, enable the strictest mode your VPN offers.

## WireGuard or OpenVPN on Windows?

A protocol decides how the VPN connection is built and encrypted, and most Windows apps let you pick one. For speed, leave the app on its default protocol, which is WireGuard-based on most VPNs. In our tests, NordVPN’s OpenVPN setting cost only a little more speed than NordLynx:

## What Is Small Business CRM Software?

If you're trying to manage your customer contacts as an entrepreneur or part of a small business with more than 50 customers in a spreadsheet, you've probably already realized this is an unwieldy task. CRM systems take the pain out of this all-important function.

CRMs have two important advantages over simple contact lists or databases. First, they add internal features that directly handle other parts of your sales funnel, notably commission management, pipelining, and scheduling.

Second, and even more important, they help move customer data back and forth between systems. Integrating your CRM with the rest of your software stack ensures that the details of every customer interaction are readily available on demand. That can include anything from lunch with a sales rep to form submissions, online chats, phone calls, and social media mentions. A sales rep can pull that data into a purchase conversation, while a help desk technician can use it to better understand a customer's situation.

## How Much Do Small Business CRMs Cost?

These types of CRMs can start at less than $10 per user per month and scale to upward of $50 per user per month. As with any subscription software, you should take advantage of free trials when available. No matter how many reviews you read or demos you watch, it's difficult to determine how well a particular CRM works until you start using it.

Your best bet is to look for a solution that is easy for non-specialists to grasp; you likely don't have time (or the budget) for lengthy, in-person training. You should also search for a product that includes FAQs, a knowledge base, and other support articles. User forums can also often be an effective support resource.

## What Can a CRM Do for Your Small Business?

A CRM can gather all your company's interactions with each customer and combine them with related data from sources such as accounting, inventory, marketing, and purchasing. This can help you maintain an accurate sales pipeline that can react quickly to new opportunities.

For example, if a help desk representative realizes a customer is ready for an upsell opportunity while addressing an unrelated support issue, a CRM ensures that insight doesn't get lost in an email. It can automatically extract that data from the ticket, add it to a record, and place the details in the pipeline so a sales manager can allocate the opportunity. Depending on how your sales department works, CRM data can appear in an app interface, an email, a Slack message, and on any device, especially mobile ones.

Even more critical than fast dissemination is intake. By automating data gathering in the CRM and every connected app, you get the data where you need it. Think of your sales pipeline as a funnel with a wide mouth at one end that grabs as much data as possible. By the time the information reaches the other end, the funnel has parsed it into useful units for the people who need it.

The primary challenge for smaller businesses is deploying and integrating CRM systems with their existing ones. This often requires significant effort from trained IT staff, who are likely to be in short supply or nonexistent at very small organizations.

## Getting Started and Ease of Use: Less Intimidating Than It Seems

During Apptivo’s onboarding process, it suggests industry-appropriate apps you can use to customize your dashboard. This helps prevent the decision paralysis you might feel when choosing from the full range of 65+ apps. You can also schedule a demo with an Apptivo specialist to help you determine which apps you need.

I installed Contacts, Customers, Invoicing, Leads, and Proposal/Price Quote to test Apptivo’s CRM capabilities. From there, Apptivo directed me to a task-oriented calendar screen. A sidebar menu here includes quick links to sections like your Apptivo inbox, call log, and task list. Other apps, like Leads and Contacts, are accessible via the top menu. This creates a highly focused experience within each app while still allowing you to quickly switch between them.

I changed the home page's Default App View to the CRM option to help me focus on lead management and opportunities (Apptivo’s version of deals). You can also modify the menu’s appearance and rearrange the apps to your preference. This level of customization is excellent, especially since Apptivo makes these options more accessible than Zoho CRM.

## Importing Customers and Employees: The Process Could Be Smoother

Next, I headed to the Leads area, where I encountered a bit of trouble. This section has a Create button but no Import button. Selecting Create opens a contact profile where you can add a full set of details, information about their behavior (including hobbies), and social media profiles. However, I still didn’t see an option to import leads.

I finally found the Import option by clicking the More button at the top right of the interface. From there, I was able to import a CSV. I didn't like having to manually map the spreadsheet to Apptivo fields, since other CRMs, such as Freshsales and Zoho CRM, automate this. Nonetheless, the fields were easy to navigate, and I completed the process in under two minutes. You can also import contacts from Gmail or Yahoo, but not from Outlook or other CRMs. This is mildly disappointing, since competing apps such as Freshsales and Zoho CRM let you import contacts from a broader range of sources.

Finally, I went to the Employees app to add team members. An employee profile consists of their name, email address, and department. You can also assign security roles to manage permissions.

Leads appear in a table view by default, but you can use the Display menu to modify the information. However, I had some trouble figuring out how to switch to the Kanban view. This wasn't the only time I had to turn to Apptivo’s documentation to figure out something that should have been intuitive. Here's how to enable that view for Leads.

Once I set up the Kanban view, I could see lead information and drag leads into new sections of the board based on their interactions. Apptivo automatically adds Leads to the Kanban board once you assign them a status, which is easy to do in the lead profile. This is a simpler process than in Zoho CRM.

Clicking on an individual lead opens a profile overlay with relevant contact information. You also see several icons at the top for tasks like emailing the lead and scheduling a follow-up. You can view more information about your interactions with a lead by clicking the More button. The level of information here is excellent, especially since you don’t have to leave the page. However, you do need to open a new page to view scheduled events and other notes, so this overlay makes for only a mild advantage over other CRMs.

Note that Apptivo distinguishes between Leads and Customers. Leads (and Contacts) are individuals, while Customers are businesses. You can connect multiple Leads or Contacts to a single Customer, which makes it easier to track interactions with several employees at a business you’re negotiating with. # Apptivo CRM
...
Apptivo provides a highly customizable, feature-rich CRM experience with all the tools and analytics your small business needs.
...
That gives it a clear advantage over Zoho CRM, which charges extra for a similar level of support. Pipedrive (starting at $14 per user per month, billed annually), meanwhile, restricts chat and phone support to higher-tier plans. However, many other CRMs, including Freshsales, match Apptivo's level of support, often at a lower price.

## Getting Started and Ease of Use: Less Intimidating Than It Seems

During Apptivo’s onboarding process, it suggests industry-appropriate apps you can use to customize your dashboard. This helps prevent the decision paralysis you might feel when choosing from the full range of 65+ apps. You can also schedule a demo with an Apptivo specialist to help you determine which apps you need.

I installed Contacts, Customers, Invoicing, Leads, and Proposal/Price Quote to test Apptivo’s CRM capabilities. From there, Apptivo directed me to a task-oriented calendar screen. A sidebar menu here includes quick links to sections like your Apptivo inbox, call log, and task list. Other apps, like Leads and Contacts, are accessible via the top menu. This creates a highly focused experience within each app while still allowing you to quickly switch between them.

I changed the home page's Default App View to the CRM option to help me focus on lead management and opportunities (Apptivo’s version of deals). You can also modify the menu’s appearance and rearrange the apps to your preference. This level of customization is excellent, especially since Apptivo makes these options more accessible than Zoho CRM.

## Importing Customers and Employees: The Process Could Be Smoother

Next, I headed to the Leads area, where I encountered a bit of trouble. This section has a Create button but no Import button. Selecting Create opens a contact profile where you can add a full set of details, information about their behavior (including hobbies), and social media profiles. However, I still didn’t see an option to import leads.

I finally found the Import option by clicking the More button at the top right of the interface. From there, I was able to import a CSV. I didn't like having to manually map the spreadsheet to Apptivo fields, since other CRMs, such as Freshsales and Zoho CRM, automate this. Nonetheless, the fields were easy to navigate, and I completed the process in under two minutes. You can also import contacts from Gmail or Yahoo, but not from Outlook or other CRMs. This is mildly disappointing, since competing apps such as Freshsales and Zoho CRM let you import contacts from a broader range of sources.

Finally, I went to the Employees app to add team members. An employee profile consists of their name, email address, and department. You can also assign security roles to manage permissions.

## Leads: Detailed Profiles That Enable Easy Management

Leads appear in a table view by default, but you can use the Display menu to modify the information. However, I had some trouble figuring out how to switch to the Kanban view. This wasn't the only time I had to turn to Apptivo’s documentation to figure out something that should have been intuitive. Here's how to enable that view for Leads.

Once I set up the Kanban view, I could see lead information and drag leads into new sections of the board based on their interactions. Apptivo automatically adds Leads to the Kanban board once you assign them a status, which is easy to do in the lead profile. This is a simpler process than in Zoho CRM.

Clicking on an individual lead opens a profile overlay with relevant contact information. You also see several icons at the top for tasks like emailing the lead and scheduling a follow-up. You can view more information about your interactions with a lead by clicking the More button. The level of information here is excellent, especially since you don’t have to leave the page. However, you do need to open a new page to view scheduled events and other notes, so this overlay makes for only a mild advantage over other CRMs.

Note that Apptivo distinguishes between Leads and Customers. Leads (and Contacts) are individuals, while Customers are businesses. You can connect multiple Leads or Contacts to a single Customer, which makes it easier to track interactions with several employees at a business you’re negotiating with. B2C companies can ignore the Customers app and focus on Leads and Contacts.

## Opportunities: All the Information You Need to Process Deals

The Opportunities section of Apptivo is where you create and manage deals. Like Leads, this area uses a table view by default, but you can switch to a Kanban view...
